title: Streaming bridge: AsyncIterable <-> Web ReadableStream adapters with retry/backpressure ergonomics
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: Our TypeScript SDK exposes streaming via an AsyncIterable (async generator) but many browser-based consumers and Web Platform integrations prefer WHATWG ReadableStream. Customers also ask for clearer retry semantics for interrupted streams and ergonomics for backpressure/abort handling.

Goals:
- Provide first-class adapter utilities to convert SDK AsyncIterable streams to ReadableStream and vice-versa (toWebStream, fromWebStream).
- Expose a simple, well-documented high-level API so consumers can choose the primitive they need without bundling polyfills by default.
- Implement pragmatic retry semantics for transient network failures during streaming where the server supports resume tokens; otherwise provide clear guidance and helper primitives for client-side replays.
- Correctly surface AbortSignal propagation and backpressure so browser consumers can apply flow control.

Non-goals:
- Implement server-side resume logic (we assume optional resume_token header support from the platform).
- Provide automatic stream replay that requires model-level deterministic resume unless the server provides tokens.

Proposed API surface (TypeScript):
- client.stream(request): AsyncIterable<StreamDelta>  // current ergonomic default
- client.streamWeb(request): ReadableStream<Uint8Array | string | StreamDelta> // new helper that wraps stream()
- utils.toWebStream(asyncIterable, { signal? }): ReadableStream // converts an AsyncIterable to a WHATWG ReadableStream
- utils.fromWebStream(readable, { signal? }): AsyncIterable // converts ReadableStream -> AsyncIterable for internal reuse and Node interop
- client.streamWithRetries(request, { maxAttempts, onRetry?(attempt, lastSeenToken) }) -> AsyncIterable  // helper that uses resume_token when available

Key implementation notes and trade-offs:
- Bundle size: adapters will be exported as an opt-in submodule ("@redwood/sdk/streaming-adapters") to avoid increasing the core SDK footprint for users who only use async iterables.
- Node vs. Browser APIs: rely on global WHATWG streams when available (Node 18+ / modern browsers). For older Node versions we provide a tiny shim that maps stream.Readable to ReadableStream if required, but this is opt-in.
- Backpressure: implement push-based loop using controller.enqueue + await when controller.desiredSize <= 0 to honour backpressure. For AsyncIterable -> ReadableStream we will pause underlying consumption when desiredSize is low.
- Abort propagation: respect AbortSignal passed by caller; when aborted we will call underlying iterator.return() if present and close the stream cleanly, including reporting an AbortError to the consumer.
- Retry semantics: two modes: 1) server-provided resume_token: on transient network error, re-issue request with resume_token to continue from last acknowledged token; 2) no resume support: emit clear error and surface helper 'replayFrom(startIdx)' utility so caller can re-request with reconstructed prompt state. We'll prefer simple deterministic helpers to avoid surprising automatic replays.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for adapter utils in Node and a browser-like environment (jsdom + web-streams-polyfill).
- Integration tests against staging streaming endpoint that supports resume_token to validate resume flow and metrics for token duplication.
- Memory/regression tests to ensure iterator->stream conversions don't accrue unbounded queues under throttled consumers.

Metrics & telemetry:
- Emit events when an adapter is used (adapter.type = "async->web" or "web->async"), when retry occurs, and when resume_token is used, for offline debugging and rollout telemetry.

Rollout plan:
- Merge behind feature flag in SDK (ENABLE_STREAMING_ADAPTERS).
- Canary release to internal infra and 10% of public installs for 2 weeks. Monitor errors, memory, and customer support tickets.
- Gradual broad release in sdk-ts-2.4.0 once no regressions seen.
acceptance_criteria: Adapter utilities toWebStream and fromWebStream implemented and exported from @redwood/sdk/streaming-adapters
client.streamWeb(request) returns a functioning ReadableStream in Node 18+ and modern browsers without polyfills
AbortSignal passed to either API aborts underlying iterator and closes stream without leaking resources
Retry helper can resume from resume_token on staging and emits telemetry events when used
Unit and integration tests added and passing in CI for Node and browser configs
Documentation and three examples (chat streaming in browser, file-download style stream, Node pipeline using stream.pipeline) added to SDK docs
